reading.body:
Every tool in this dataset targets a domain where a wrong output carries legal or financial liability, which makes the risk notes more informative than the feature descriptions.

The six tools split roughly into two clusters. Three operate on legal documents, contract language, and case research, and each one carries a note about privilege, confidentiality, or work-product exposure. Two work on financial data and market intelligence, and both flag risks tied to proprietary data handling and trading decisions, including the specific concern of material non-public information. The sixth, Vanta, sits apart as a compliance monitoring tool rather than an analytical one. All six vendors are US-based, so the dataset says nothing about how these problems are being approached in other jurisdictions.

The pattern that matters is that sensitivity of the underlying data, not sophistication of the model, appears to be the governing constraint for deployment in both fields. A legal AI that surfaces privileged communications or a finance AI that influences a trade on improperly handled data creates regulatory exposure that no accuracy benchmark resolves. The risk notes attached to every entry here reflect that reality. What the data does not cover is compute footprint, inference cost, or power demand, so no connection to infrastructure constraints can be drawn from it.
